title: At Risk trend line has twelve monthly points and the last equals the count
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission and can reverse an invoice, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide at 100% zoom (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  • {Location-A} has invoices going back more than a year, with many customers.
  • The At Risk Customers tile's window pill reads 120 Days.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Lapsed Fleet) is at risk on 120 days: its newest invoice, on work order {Work-order-1} (for example S490-1180), is 2 to 6 months old, and it also has an older invoice.
  • {Work-order-1}'s invoice has no payment, so it can be reversed.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top bar.
  2. Take a screenshot of the At Risk Customers tile and read its headline.
  3. Count the points on the At Risk Customers trend line, from left to right.
  4. Hover over each point and write down the month and the value it shows.
  5. Click Work Orders, open {Work-order-1}, click the Finance tab, click the invoice's three dots, click Reverse and confirm.
  6. Click Dashboard in the top bar and check the At Risk Customers pill still reads 120 Days.
  7. Hover over each point again, write down the month and the value, and read the headline.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: The trend line has twelve points, one per month, for the last twelve months.
  • Step 4: The right-most point's value equals the headline from step 2 (for example both 12).
  • Step 7: At least one earlier month's value differs from what you wrote down in step 4, not only the last one: every point is worked out again from today's data rather than kept from the past.
  • Step 7: The right-most point's value still equals the headline.
  • Steps 4 and 7: If the points show no value when you hover them, the values cannot be checked by hand, because the line's height does not show the count (each tile draws its line between its own lowest and highest point). Write "point values not checked by hand" in the result comment and mark the case Blocked.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9577 (Story 5, Count Tiles), with SV-9576 (Story 4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S5-R13 (unchanged since version 42) and S4-R11b (added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 (15:06 UTC) by Chris Ward, from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026 to our question sheet; the spec's change log (version 46) lists it under 2026-10-14); read 14 Oct 2026. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge) boards 01_Opens_After and 09_AtRisk_After, used for on-screen labels only. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R13: “The At Risk Customers sparkline shows the at-risk count over the trailing twelve months as twelve monthly points. Each historical point is the at-risk count as of the last day of that month in the workplace's timezone, using the inactivity window the tile currently shows. The twelfth point is computed as of now, rather than as of a month end that has not happened yet, so it always equals the headline. Every point is recomputed from current data, so a later void changes the past points: recording the count as it stood at the time would contradict S3-E2, which excludes a voided invoice even when deciding a customer's most recent invoice.”
  • S4-R11b: “The sparkline shows direction, not level. Each tile scales its line between its own lowest and highest point, so a figure that never changes over the range (for example Technician Utilization at 100% on every day) draws as a flat line along the bottom of the trend area, whatever the figure is. The headline carries the actual value. The start-at-0 axis of S9-R8 applies to the expanded and report charts, which have an axis, not to the sparkline.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
